source_acquisition.search_note: The inventory row is no_public_source_found and corpus/visual_sources/icml-2026-35879ec17414/ is empty. The PDF footnote explicitly links the official repository, whose title/README match the paper but whose tree contains only implementation and runner files, with no plot, figure, table, LaTeX, TikZ, PGF, SVG, notebook, style, or visual-data source. A strict-title reproduction candidate (will-rice/icml-2026-reproductions) was checked with gh and likewise has no visual source files; its evidence states that the paper’s broader evaluations were not rerun. Figure typography, color, and line widths therefore remain rendered estimates rather than source-exact claims.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Figures 1–2 reuse a four-color categorical method palette (Min-p, Top-p, Top-H, Top-W); Figure 3 switches to a three-color categorical λ palette. Tables are black-and-white and use bold maxima and group rules rather than cell color. Structural black/gray is not counted as a semantic series color.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Text, table rules, captions, and table values are PDF text/line objects; Figures 1–3 are embedded raster images (Figures 1–2 about 260 dpi and Figure 3 panels about 977 dpi according to pdfimages).
paper_style.style_consistency: Two-column letter layout, cross-column objects, below-object captions, Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern document typography, and partial-grid tables are consistent. Figure 1/2 reuse a coherent bar grammar, while the sans-serif raster figures use smaller estimated text and do not expose source-level settings.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. Alpaca accuracy across temperatures for Min-p, Top-p, Top-H, and Top-W (aggregated over 4 runs). As we can see in the bar plot, Min-p, Top-p, Top-H and Top-W (our method) win in 0,1,2,12 tuples of (T, model) out of 15 tuples, i.e., 5 temperatures × 3 models, respectively.

color.semantic_mapping: Min-p=#5095C4, Top-p=#FF9B43, Top-H=#5AB55A, Top-W=#DF5657; black/gray are structural text, axes, and grid.

encodings.x: temperature T at five categorical values (0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0)
encodings.y: Alpaca result value, labelled Accuracy (%) in the plot
encodings.color: sampling method: Min-p, Top-p, Top-H, Top-W
encodings.text: panel titles, temperature ticks, two-decimal values above bars, and shared method legend

figures.data_and_statistics: Three models × five temperatures × four methods yield 60 aggregate bars. The caption states aggregation over 4 runs; the paper describes AlpacaEval as a length-controlled win rate, but the caption and y-axis call it accuracy. No bar-level standard deviation, interval, or failure count is displayed.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 5 evaluation protocol and Section 6.1 AlpacaEval results support the cross-temperature stability comparison; the plot is compared with Figure 2 and Table 3 and carries headline and main-comparison evidence.
design_strengths: Shared temperature and method order across three model facets makes stability comparisons fast.
One shared legend, panel titles, and direct bar labels reduce lookup cost.
The palette and layout are reused by Figure 2, preserving a common judge-result vocabulary.
design_weaknesses: Method identity is almost entirely color-coded, so grayscale and color-vision-limited reading is weak.
Sixty two-decimal labels become crowded at page scale and no cell-level uncertainty is shown.
Accuracy terminology in the caption and axis is inconsistent with the AlpacaEval win-rate definition in the body.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a two-row small-multiple grouped-bar layout for model × temperature, with a shared method legend, stable palette, and direct values; add shape or line-style redundancy and harmonize the metric name and uncertainty in the caption.

evidence.label: Figure 1. Alpaca accuracy across temperatures for Min-p, Top-p, Top-H, and Top-W

color.semantic_mapping: Min-p=#5095C4, Top-p=#FF9B43, Top-H=#5AB55A, Top-W=#DF5657; black/gray are structural text, axes, and grid.

encodings.x: temperature T at five categorical values (0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0)
encodings.y: MT-Bench judge score on the paper's 1–10 scale, but plotted as Accuracy (%)
encodings.color: sampling method: Min-p, Top-p, Top-H, Top-W
encodings.text: panel titles, temperature ticks, two-decimal values above bars, and shared method legend

figures.data_and_statistics: Three models × five temperatures × four methods yield 60 aggregate bars. The caption states aggregation over 4 runs and the body defines MT-Bench as an average judge score on a 1–10 scale. No standard deviation, interval, error bar, or failure count is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 5 MT-Bench judge protocol and Section 6.1 results support a second headline comparison; Figure 2 reuses Figure 1 to compare judge behavior and is read with Table 3 creative scores.
design_strengths: Reusing Figure 1 panel, temperature, method order, and palette makes the two judge tasks directly comparable.
Direct values expose small differences and the caption reports the 15-cell winner count.
The temperature sweep makes high-temperature Top-p degradation visible across model facets.
design_weaknesses: The y-axis label Accuracy (%) is incompatible with the MT-Bench 1–10 judge-score definition.
Color is the only method identity cue and the 60 labels are crowded at reduced scale.
Four-run aggregation is stated without run dispersion, so winner counts can hide close or heterogeneous cells.
figures.reusable_pattern: Keep a common small-multiple frame and method palette across tasks, but synchronize the y-axis unit and caption with each metric and add uncertainty or an auditable cell-level summary beside aggregate bars.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.module: ablation / Section 6.2 Top-W Ablations and Behavior

caption.text: Figure 3. GSM8K accuracy sensitivity of Top-W to β for fixed λs and LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct at T ∈ {1.0, 1.5, 2.0}.

color.semantic_mapping: lam=1.0 uses #1F77B4, lam=2.0 uses #FF7F0E, and lam=3.0 uses #2CA02C; black/gray are axes and grid.

encodings.x: β on a linear sweep with visible ticks from 0 to 7
encodings.y: GSM8K accuracy on a linear 0.0–0.8 scale

figures.data_and_statistics: The figure fixes LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct and GSM8K, sweeps β for λ∈{1.0,2.0,3.0}, and facets by T∈{1.0,1.5,2.0}. Each curve is an accuracy trajectory; no repeat count, mean, standard deviation, interval, denominator, or failure value is displayed.
figures.evidence_relation: Theorem 3.4/Corollary 3.5 and Section 4.4 motivate β monotonicity and tuning; this ablation links those controls to observed GSM8K sensitivity and is read with Tables 3 and 8, but does not visualize global convergence or candidate-pool exactness.
design_strengths: All three facets share β and accuracy scales, enabling temperature-dependent sensitivity comparison.
λ as curves and T as facets map directly to the two control parameters discussed in the method.
Circular points and connecting lines expose discrete curve shape rather than only a winner count.
design_weaknesses: Repeated legends consume plotting area and color remains the main λ cue, weakening grayscale reading.
Small raster ticks and legends are hard to read at page scale and no uncertainty distinguishes signal from run noise.
The caption omits the concrete λ values and leaves the mapping to the in-panel legends and body text.
figures.reusable_pattern: Put one tuning parameter on a shared x-axis, a second in line/marker series, and a third in facets; add line-style or marker redundancy and state all fixed values and uncertainty conventions in the caption.

evidence.label: Figure 3. GSM8K accuracy sensitivity of Top-W to β

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1. GSM8K accuracy (%) at T ∈ {0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0} for Min-p, Top-p, Top-H, and Top-W. Aggregated over 3 runs (N=1319).

tables.uncertainty: GSM8K exact-match accuracy (%) aggregated over 3 runs (N=1319); no cell-level SD, SE, interval, or failure column.
tables.data_and_statistics: Three models × five temperatures × four methods provide 60 cells. The table reports the QA main comparison and the caption supplies the aggregate run count.
tables.evidence_relation: Section 5 matched evaluation protocol → GSM8K main comparison → Section 6.1 winner-count claim and Figure 3 β sensitivity.
design_strengths: Grouped model-to-method headers and common temperature rows make cross-model comparisons direct.
Fixed decimal precision and bold group maxima support rapid scanning without cell colors.
design_weaknesses: Three-run aggregation hides run variation; 13 columns remain dense and some baseline values are cited rather than independently generated.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use model→method grouped headers and common temperature rows for multi-model decoding results, while retaining per-cell dispersion or a reproducible source alongside the aggregate.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2. GPQA accuracy at T ∈ {0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0} for Min-p, Top-p, Top-H, and Top-W. Aggregated over 4 runs (N = 448).

tables.uncertainty: GPQA accuracy aggregated over 4 runs (N = 448); no cell-level standard deviation, standard error, interval, or failure column.
tables.data_and_statistics: The same 60-cell model × temperature × method grid tests whether the comparison extends from GSM8K to a knowledge-oriented benchmark.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 1 GSM8K comparison → Table 2 GPQA comparison → Section 6.1 robustness and high-temperature stability claim.
design_strengths: Grouped model-to-method headers and common temperature rows make cross-model comparisons direct.
Fixed decimal precision and bold group maxima support rapid scanning without cell colors.
design_weaknesses: No cell-level uncertainty is shown; the wide table is information-dense and the caption omits the detailed GPQA answer-extraction convention.
tables.reusable_pattern: Reuse the isomorphic table grammar across benchmarks, aligning temperature and method rows and stating units, extraction protocol, repeats, and denominator in the caption.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3. Average judge score (mean ± std over repeats) for each temperature T and prompt. For each (T, prompt) and model, the best (highest mean) method is bolded; ties are bolded for all maxima. For details on each of the, Diversity, Originality, Narrative Flow, Emotional Impact check the Appendix. Across all 27 triplets, Min-p, top-p, and Top-H win 8, 5, and 5 cases respectively, while Top-W wins 9. This experiment is conducted under β = 2.8 with similar settings as other experiments.

tables.uncertainty: Each cell is mean ± std over repeats for a 1–10 LLM-as-a-Judge score; five creative dimensions are summarized by Avg. The caption reports winner counts Min-p=8/27, Top-p=5/27, Top-H=5/27, Top-W=9/27 under default β=2.8.
tables.data_and_statistics: Three temperatures × three prompts × three models × four methods form 27 temperature–prompt–model triplets, with mean and standard deviation shown for each method.
tables.evidence_relation: Section 5 creative rubric → default-β aggregate in Table 3 → Appendix Tables 5–7 model details and Table 8 high-β variant.
design_strengths: Model and method groups, means, dispersion, tie rule, winner denominator, and β setting coexist in one main-text table.
The aggregate view gives a compact bridge from the headline results to the appendix rubric details.
design_weaknesses: Approximately 6.67 pt body text and 14 columns are hard to read; M1–M5 are not expanded and the caption contains the incomplete phrase “For details on each of the,”.
Winner counts remain an aggregate conclusion and require Appendix M for rubric heterogeneity.
tables.reusable_pattern: Organize multi-axis judge means with model→method grouped columns, explicit mean ± std, tie rules, parameter settings, and winner denominators; include the rubric dictionary in a header or caption when possible.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4. Decoding speed (milliseconds per generated token, ms/tok) for different sampling methods across temperatures.

tables.uncertainty: Decoding speed in milliseconds per generated token (ms/tok) for three models, two temperatures, and four methods; no hardware, repeat count, dispersion, or failure information is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: The table provides 24 runtime cells and supports the paper’s approximately 5.4% average overhead statement.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix K complexity theorem → measured decoding speed → Section 6.2 overhead discussion; it is the only direct cost evidence.
design_strengths: Model groups carry the unit and the temperature/method alignment makes absolute speed comparisons easy.
Four decimal places expose small millisecond differences.
design_weaknesses: Hardware, batch size, warm-up, repeat protocol, and dispersion are absent, so values are hard to interpret outside the reported environment.
The 13-column layout is dense and there is no relative-overhead column.
tables.reusable_pattern: Pair absolute ms/token with a relative baseline cost and state hardware, warm-up, batch, repetitions, and summarization in the caption or adjacent metadata.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5. LLM-as-a-Judge creative-writing scores for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Each entry is mean ± std over 5 repeats; higher is better. For each (temperature, prompt), the maximum value in each metric column is bolded (ties broken by method order: Top-p, Min-p, Top-H, Top-W ).

tables.uncertainty: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct creative-writing M1–M5 and Avg scores are mean ± std over 5 repeats; higher is better and there is no failure column.
tables.data_and_statistics: The 36 rows expand three temperatures × three prompts × four methods for one model, retaining five rubric dimensions and their average.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 3 aggregate → LLaMA model-specific rubric detail → Table 8 high-β aggregate.
design_strengths: A common long-table schema keeps temperature, prompt, method, five dimensions, and Avg aligned across models.
Mean ± std and the maximum/tie-breaking rule are explicit in the caption.
design_weaknesses: The approximately 6.67 pt body and 36 rows impose high lookup cost.
M1–M5 remain abstract column names and judge/prompt dependence requires Appendix M.1.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use temperature→prompt→method row nesting for model-specific judge detail, preserving method order and putting all rubric dimensions and dispersion in one comparable long table.

tables.uncertainty: Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct creative-writing M1–M5 and Avg scores are mean ± std over 5 repeats; no failure or exclusion column is reported.

tables.evidence_relation: Table 3 cross-model aggregate → Phi model detail → Table 8 high-β three-model comparison.
design_strengths: A common long-table schema keeps temperature, prompt, method, five dimensions, and Avg aligned across models.
Mean ± std and the maximum/tie-breaking rule are explicit in the caption.
design_weaknesses: Small text and 36 rows create scan burden; M1–M5 are unexplained in the table and there is no judge-agreement, prompt-level uncertainty, or failure summary.

caption.text: Table 7. LLM-as-a-Judge creative-writing scores for Qwen2.5-3B. Each entry is mean ± std over 5 repeats; higher is better. For each (temperature, prompt), the maximum value in each metric column is bolded (ties broken by method order: Top-p, Min-p, Top-H, Top-W ).

tables.uncertainty: Qwen2.5-3B creative-writing M1–M5 and Avg scores are mean ± std over 5 repeats; higher is better and no failure/exclusion column is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: The 36 rows expand three temperatures × three prompts × four methods for Qwen and show each rubric dimension plus Avg.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 3 aggregate → Qwen model-specific detail → Table 8 high-β aggregate.
design_strengths: A common long-table schema keeps temperature, prompt, method, five dimensions, and Avg aligned across models.
Mean ± std and the maximum/tie-breaking rule are explicit in the caption.

tables.label: Table 8

caption.text: Table 8. Average judge score (mean ± std over repeats) for each temperature T and prompt, comparing four sampling methods on three base models. For each (T, prompt) and model, the best (highest mean) method is bolded; ties are bolded for all maxima. For details on each of the, Diversity, Originality, Narrative Flow, Emotional Impact check the Appendix. Across all 27 triplets, Min-p, top-p, and Top-H win 6, 5, and 5 cases respectively, while Top-W wins 12. (This experiment is done under β(T ) = 1.5 + 1.5T while keeping the rest of parameters the same. In this experiment, β is higher than the default of this paper which is β = 2.8 and we can see that higher β can actually help depending on dataset and type of experiment such as when we value Diversity, Originality, Narrative Flow, Emotional Impact check, all together.)

tables.uncertainty: Avg judge score is mean ± std over repeats for three models × three temperatures × three prompts × four methods. Top-W uses β(T)=1.5+1.5T while other parameters stay fixed; winner counts are Min-p=6, Top-p=5, Top-H=5, Top-W=12.
tables.data_and_statistics: The 9 rows summarize 27 temperature–prompt–model triplets and display only Avg, not the five rubric dimensions.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 3 default β=2.8 aggregate → Table 8 high-β(T) variant → Appendix Tables 5–7 dimension-level detail.
design_strengths: A compact 14-column table places three models, three temperatures, three prompts, four methods, mean ± std, schedule, and winner counts in one comparison.
The variant is directly juxtaposed with the default-β aggregate, making the parameter boundary visible.
design_weaknesses: The long caption contains the incomplete phrase “For details on each of the,” and its high-β condition is not directly comparable to default β without careful reading.
The approximately 6.67 pt table shows only Avg, so rubric-level heterogeneity remains hidden and the high-β winner count can mask the changed condition.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a compact aggregate table to compare default and variant settings, explicitly marking which cells share an experimental condition and retaining winner counts alongside per-cell mean ± std.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Tables 1–2 establish the temperature × model QA grid; Figures 1–2 reuse grouped bars for two judge tasks; Table 3 gives the default-β creative aggregate; Figure 3 exposes β/λ/T sensitivity; Appendix Table 4 connects complexity to runtime, Tables 5–7 expand model-level creative rubrics, and Table 8 tests a high-β(T) variant. Equations and Algorithm 1 carry the W1/entropy/mass mechanism, so visual objects emphasize outcomes rather than geometry or convergence diagnostics.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Every object uses an italicized Figure/Table label followed by a below-object explanatory caption. Figures 1–2 and Tables 3/8 include winner counts; Tables 3/5–8 define mean ± std or repeats. Metric naming degrades in Figure 1/2, and the rubric pointer phrase in Tables 3/8 is incomplete.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables 1–2, 4, and 8 use two-level model→sampling-method column groups; Table 3 combines temperature/prompt row indices with model→method columns; Tables 5–7 use temperature→prompt→sampling rows and M1–M5/Avg columns. Partial horizontal rules and bold group maxima replace full grids and cell color.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Sections 3–4, the fixed-f prefix theorem, and Algorithm 1 have no companion mechanism diagram. Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–2 carry main comparisons, Tables 3/5–8 carry judge evidence, Figure 3 and Table 8 carry β sensitivity/variant evidence, and Table 4 carries cost evidence; geometry, candidate-pool exactness, and alternating convergence are not visually diagnosed.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main-text Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–3 provide aggregate headline and ablation views. Appendix Table 4 carries the complexity-to-speed check, Tables 5–7 carry the Appendix M.1 rubric decomposition, and Table 8 extends Table 3 under β(T). The unnumbered gray prompt boxes on p.16 provide rubric context but are not Figure/Table objects.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Document text and captions use Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern consistently, but table body size falls from about 9.33 pt in Tables 1–2 to about 6.67 pt in Table 3 and Tables 5–8. The three raster figures use an estimated DejaVu Sans face with small in-plot labels. No public visual source permits exact rcParams or export-size verification.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Figures 1–2 share four method colors, creating a stable result vocabulary; Figure 3 uses three λ colors and tables remain monochrome. All figures lack sufficient shape/line-style redundancy for grayscale, while table bolding and grouping supply non-color comparison cues.

most_reusable_patterns: Two-row, three-model × five-temperature grouped-bar small multiples with a shared method legend, stable palette, and direct bar values.
Model→method grouped table headers with temperature/prompt row indices and bold group maxima.
Layered creative evidence: main-text aggregate Table 3, per-model long Tables 5–7, and high-β aggregate Table 8.
β on the x-axis, λ as line series, and temperature as facets for a compact sensitivity view.
highest_value_objects: Table 1: the isomorphic temperature/model/method GSM8K grid directly supports the high-temperature stability claim.
Figures 1 and 2: the shared panel grammar and palette enable rapid cross-task comparison of model/temperature heterogeneity.
Tables 3 and 8: default-β and high-β(T) aggregates bound the creative-quality claim by parameter condition.
Figure 3: the only direct β/λ/T visual link between control-parameter discussion and observed accuracy trajectories.
failure_patterns: Method or λ identity is mainly color-coded in every figure, with weak grayscale and color-vision robustness.
Figure 2 labels MT-Bench judge scores as Accuracy (%), while Figure 1’s Alpaca accuracy wording conflicts with the body’s win-rate definition.
The approximately 6.67 pt Table 3 and Tables 5–8 text and abstract M1–M5 columns force repeated appendix navigation.
QA aggregates and Figures 1–2 omit cell-level dispersion, so run counts and winner counts can conceal close or heterogeneous cells.
Figure 3 is a small raster panel with repeated legends and no uncertainty; no public plot/table/LaTeX source permits source-level reproduction.
Table 8’s very long, partially malformed caption and changed β schedule make default/high-β winner counts easy to over-compare.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Use consistent three-model grouped bars to establish the temperature result spine, model→method mean ± std long tables to retain judge detail, and β–λ–T small multiples to expose control sensitivity; repair source availability, metric labels, and grayscale redundancy in the next version.
